pointers.sentence: Most of Django's own are in `django/views/decorators/`, among them `require_http_methods`, `never_cache`, `condition` and `csrf_exempt`.

`require_GET` and `vary_on_cookie` are the result of such a call kept under a name, so the wrappers they put around the masthead are made by `require_http_methods` and `vary_on_headers` (`django/views/decorators/http.py:require_GET`, `django/views/decorators/vary.py:vary_on_cookie`, `django/views/decorators/cache.py:cache_control`).

The wrapper that `require_http_methods` makes compares the request's method with its list, and if the method is not there it returns an `HttpResponseNotAllowed` naming the list, logs a warning, and never calls what it wraps (`django/views/decorators/http.py:require_http_methods`).

The docstring asks for the methods in upper case, and nothing converts the list (`django/views/decorators/http.py:require_http_methods`, `django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:WSGIRequest.__init__`, `django/core/handlers/asgi.py:ASGIRequest.__init__`).

The masthead's other two wrappers each call inwards, take the response that comes back, and edit its headers before returning it; what they write, and how it merges with a header already there, is told in [Cache headers and conditional requests: `django/utils/cache.py`](../services/http-caching.md) (`django/views/decorators/vary.py:vary_on_headers`, `django/views/decorators/cache.py:never_cache`).

The one picked is passed through `functools.wraps`, which copies the view's name, docstring and attributes onto it, so that a mark set by a decorator further in reaches the function the URLconf holds ([What the handler asks of a view](callable.md#what-other-code-reads-from-a-view)) (`django/views/decorators/cache.py:never_cache`).

`condition` is one: it may answer with a 304, so `vary_on_cookie` written under it runs only when the view does, and written over it patches the 304 as well ([Cache headers and conditional requests: `django/utils/cache.py`](../services/http-caching.md#under-the-condition-decorator)) (`django/views/decorators/http.py:condition`).

*The view decorators of `django/views/decorators/` that are not made from a middleware, by when each changes the request or the response.
If the client already holds the current version and the request is a `"GET"` or a `"HEAD"`, the answer is a 304 and the view is never called (`django/views/decorators/http.py:condition`).

How `get_conditional_response` compares the versions, and when it answers with a 412, is told in [Cache headers and conditional requests: `django/utils/cache.py`](../services/http-caching.md#get_conditional_response).

`ConditionalGetMiddleware` makes the same decision for a `"GET"`, but from the finished response, and so only after the view has done its work (`django/middleware/http.py:ConditionalGetMiddleware.process_response`).

`csrf_exempt` and `no_append_slash` return a wrapper that does nothing but call the view, and set an attribute on the wrapper, `"csrf_exempt"` or `"should_append_slash"` (`django/views/decorators/csrf.py:csrf_exempt`, `django/views/decorators/common.py:no_append_slash`).

`csrf_exempt` and `no_append_slash` return a wrapper that does nothing but call the view, and set an attribute on the wrapper, `"csrf_exempt"` or `"should_append_slash"` (`django/views/decorators/csrf.py:csrf_exempt`, `django/views/decorators/common.py:no_append_slash`).

`non_atomic_requests`, in `django/db/transaction.py`, marks its wrapper in the same way, with `"_non_atomic_requests"`, a set of database aliases, which a second use of the decorator copies with its own added (`django/db/transaction.py:_non_atomic_requests`).

Setting the attribute on the view itself would work as well, and the comment at the head of `csrf_exempt` and of `no_append_slash` says so; each returns a new function because, in that comment's words, "decorators are nicer if they don't have side effects" (`django/views/decorators/csrf.py:csrf_exempt`, `django/views/decorators/common.py:no_append_slash`).

`csp_override` and `csp_report_only_override` each store a policy on the response, which `ContentSecurityPolicyMiddleware.process_response` uses in place of the one in the settings (`django/views/decorators/clickjacking.py:xframe_options_exempt`, `django/views/decorators/csp.py:_make_csp_decorator`).

`sensitive_post_parameters` marks the request, each time the view is called, with the posted fields an error report is not to show ([What an error report hides](report-filter.md#sensitive_variables-and-sensitive_post_parameters)) (`django/views/decorators/debug.py:sensitive_post_parameters`).
